judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 3247, which barred a public school from denying any child a free public education through secondary school, or excluding a child from a program or activity, because of the child's or a parent's or guardian's actual or perceived citizenship or immigration status, barred policies whose effect is to exclude a child from programs or a parent from parental-engagement activities on those grounds, required every school to adopt a compliance policy and to write procedures by July 1, 2026 for reviewing requests by law enforcement agents seeking to enter a school, and created a private right of action within two years of a violation with actual damages available for a willful violation. The Illinois House passed it 70-40 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 2436, which broadened the immigration cases the public defender may handle in counties over 3,000,000 people. Representation had been confined to immigration courts sitting inside the county; the bill extended it to cases arising or heard within the county and to county residents whose immigration cases are heard outside it, while leaving the county board's existing power to authorize representation beyond those limits. The Illinois House passed it 68-41 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 5093, which expanded eligibility for in-state tuition at Illinois public universities and community colleges by removing the condition tied to attending an Illinois high school or community college while residing in the state and not having established residency elsewhere before enrolling. The Illinois House passed this version 71-37. The Senate then added an exclusion for people whose nonimmigrant status precludes an intent to reside permanently in the United States, extended state financial-aid eligibility by redefining Illinois resident in the Retention of Illinois Students and Equity Act, and delayed the university changes to the 2027-2028 academic year; the House agreed to that version, which became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 5024, which barred locating, constructing, or operating a detention center facility within 1,500 feet of the property boundary of a school, day care center or home, cemetery, public park, forest preserve, public housing, private residence, or place of religious worship, regardless of the address used. As passed, the definition of a detention center facility covers facilities of units of government as well as of federal immigration authorities. The Illinois House passed it 72-35 and it became law.

As passed, the definition of a detention center facility covers facilities of units of government as well as of federal immigration authorities. The Illinois House passed it 72-35 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 1312, which created the Illinois Bivens Act letting any person sue someone who, while conducting civil immigration enforcement, knowingly engages in conduct violating the Illinois or United States Constitution, with qualified immunity preserved as a defense. The bill also created a privilege from civil arrest for people going to, attending, or returning from a state court proceeding, barred employers from retaliating against employees who report violations of the new Act, required hospitals to adopt and file a policy governing interactions with law enforcement agents involved in civil immigration activity, barred public colleges from disclosing or threatening to disclose a person's actual or perceived citizenship or immigration status and from treating immigration status or national origin as directory information, and barred licensed day care centers from admitting a law enforcement agent for immigration enforcement without valid identification and a signed judicial warrant, order, or subpoena. The Illinois Senate passed it 40-18 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 2568, the Equality for Every Family Act, which declared it state policy that a child has the same parentage rights and protections regardless of the parents' marital status, age, gender, gender identity, or sexual orientation, or the circumstances of the child's birth including assisted reproduction and surrogacy. The bill broadened who may sign an acknowledgment of parentage, revised when genetic testing may be used, let a surrogacy parentage proceeding be filed in any county and set requirements for a valid gestational surrogacy agreement, and created a confirmatory adoption process for children born through assisted reproduction. The Illinois Senate passed it 36-19 and it became law.

The Illinois Senate passed it 36-19 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4758, which barred an employer or employment agency from stating in a job posting that an applicant must hold a valid driver's license unless driving is an essential function of the posted job and a business necessity, and required a posting that does require one to briefly explain why. The version that passed reaches job postings only; an earlier draft would also have barred refusing to hire or otherwise discriminating against applicants who lack a licence, and that provision was removed before either chamber voted. The Illinois House passed it 82-30 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4379, which extended the Equitable Restrooms Act's adult changing station requirement beyond state-owned buildings to certain privately owned public buildings constructed on or after January 1, 2029, required owners to maintain and clean the stations and to leave enough floor space to meet Americans with Disabilities Act standards, and required conspicuous signage at restroom entrances. The Illinois House passed this version 72-18. The Senate then reworked which buildings count, bringing in buildings at places of education designed for 1,500 or more students and excluding athletic stadiums, and the House agreed to that version, which became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 1836, the Clean Slate Act, which established procedures for automatically sealing eligible criminal records, extended sealing to municipal ordinance violations and Class C misdemeanors, broadened which records are eligible and revised when they become eligible, removed the bar on sealing where the petitioner has a later felony conviction in specified circumstances, repealed the requirement that a petitioner attach a negative drug test, and required reporting entities to respond to notices of missing or erroneous arrest and disposition data. judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 2437, which required hospitals with licensed obstetric beds and birthing centers to adopt written policies, within six months, letting a Medicaid patient have a Medicaid-enrolled doula of their choice accompany them before, during, and after childbirth without counting against any support-person limit. The bill also extended medical assistance to foreign-born victims of human trafficking, torture, and other serious crimes and their family members, added coverage for over-the-counter choline supplements during pregnancy, required quarterly reporting on compliance with the existing ban on prior authorization for FDA-approved mental-illness drugs, and created the Certified Family Health Aide Program letting a legally responsible caregiver be certified to provide nursing-type care. The Illinois House passed it 76-39 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 3487, which required every licensed hospital to replace the age cutoffs in its influenza and pneumococcal immunization policy with procedures identifying all patients clinically eligible for those vaccines, to offer influenza immunization from September 1 through April 1 and pneumococcal immunization on admission or discharge, and to follow the most recent State Guidelines for Communicable Disease Prevention or the federal Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices recommendations, with the state guidelines controlling where the federal guidance significantly departs from evidence-based immunization practice. The Illinois Senate passed it 37-19 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 2164, which strengthened Department of Labor collection of unpaid wages by raising the non-waivable administrative fee an employer owes on a violation, making a final administrative decision a debt due and owed to the state that is collectible by all available remedies and enforceable like a civil judgment, and providing that the existing monthly damages and daily penalty keep accruing on underpayments until the order becomes such a debt. The Illinois Senate passed it 37-19 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4844, which required employers with more than 25 employees to pay an employee at the employee's regular rate of pay for time spent serving on jury duty. Employers with 25 or fewer employees are exempt. The Illinois House passed it 69-34 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 1189, which extended the Prevailing Wage Act to all federal construction projects administered or controlled by an Illinois public body, in localities where the Illinois prevailing rate equals or exceeds the federal prevailing wage determination for the same locality and type of construction. The Illinois House passed it 82-28 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4725, which required the Attorney General to investigate before bringing a worker-protection action and gave that office express investigative powers: document subpoenas, written answers to interrogatories under oath, inspection of employer premises and copying of employment records kept there, and interviews with workers at the premises. The bill also created a court process for a subpoena recipient to challenge a subpoena, set out administrative inspection warrant procedures under a reasonableness standard, let an employer refuse access to areas not open to the public without such a warrant, and exempted the material gathered from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. The Illinois House passed it 79-23 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 5090, the Transportation Network Driver Labor Relations Act, which gave rideshare drivers the right to self-organize, to form or join a driver organization, and to bargain collectively, required the Illinois Labor Relations Board to certify an exclusive bargaining representative for the driver unit and required covered companies to bargain over mandatory subjects, set out unfair work practice rules and impasse procedures, and imposed a per-trip fee on every trip originating in Illinois payable into a new Rideshare Workers Support Fund. The Illinois Senate passed it 42-12 and it became law.

The Illinois Senate passed it 42-12 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4418, which required the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency, one year after the Act took effect, to develop and begin implementing stormwater pollution prevention plan requirements, or comparable best management practice requirements, controlling plastic pellets and other preproduction plastic materials in stormwater runoff, and to write those requirements into the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permits it issues to covered industrial facilities. The Illinois House passed it 69-33 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 3026, which added a Dual Language Education Article to the School Code requiring the State Board of Education to adopt comprehensive guidance for districts on starting and expanding dual language programs by December 15, 2026, to establish recognition pathways for biliteracy below high school by July 1, 2027 with district participation optional, and by July 1, 2029 to build dual language education into its strategic equity plan including provisions for recruiting, developing, and retaining bilingual educators. The Illinois House passed it 77-35 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass S.B. 191, which required that, beginning July 1, 2031, each designated seating position in a newly purchased school bus have a lap-and-shoulder seat belt system in good operating condition meeting applicable federal standards. Buses leased by a district are exempt, as are out-of-state buses used for student activities, and the bill expressly imposes no duty on a school, district, or contractor to ensure a belt is correctly fastened or to instruct riders in using one. The Illinois Senate passed it 39-13 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4571, which let counties over 750,000 and under 2 million residents, and county-executive counties over 650,000, acquire real property to create or preserve affordable housing, donate or lease or sell county property below market rate for that purpose and choose the purchasers and lessees, offer developers grants and loans, and treat infrastructure work that increases affordable housing supply as a public-purpose improvement. The bill defines the housing it supports as reaching households earning up to 140% of area median income. The Illinois House passed it 76-33 and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass H.B. 4456, which let the Illinois Commerce Commission approve a low-income discount covering a qualifying residential customer's entire electric or gas bill including delivery and supply charges, and required any electric or gas utility serving more than 100,000 Illinois customers that lacks a compliant discount to file a tariff creating one within 30 days. The bill also directed the Commission to weigh maximizing federal and state energy assistance funds, and provided that a charge funding the discount be assessed on a fixed per-customer basis rather than by usage. The Illinois House passed it 74-37 and it became law.
